title: It is a Privilege to Collaborate with the U.S. Government on Resolving the Nature of UAP

--

The fundamental challenge in resolving the nature of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) lies with acquiring definitive evidence beyond any reasonable doubt. The quality of the scientific data must be good enough to make skeptics sound unreasonable. A single high-resolution image of a UAP or direct access to UAP materials is worth more than a million blurry images or eight billion likes on social media. How can we get that data?

One way is to check the archives of the U.S. government. The Pentagon, the Intelligence Community, the Space Command and the FBI have been collecting enormous data over the past century for the benefit of national security. This database is much larger than all the data collected by astronomical observatories in human history, because the funding allocated to collect it exceeds the funding for science by at least two orders of magnitude. Despite this data collection being motivated by down-to-Earth concerns, it could reveal a new cosmic truth akin to finding a package in our mailbox. Such a finding would inform us that we are not at the top of the cosmic food chain because the senders of the package managed to reach us before we reached them. This would bring a much-needed sense of cosmic modesty to our long-term priorities. International politics will be dwarfed by interplanetary politics.

The U.S. government already made cosmic discoveries. In the 1960s, the Vela satellites attempted to verify the compliance of the Soviet Union with the Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty, and discovered gamma-ray bursts as the birth sites of black holes at the edge of the observable universe (as reviewed here).

Of course, we do not need the U.S. government to tell us about unusual objects in the sky. We can simply look up. The sky is not classified. Only the most advanced sensors operated by the U.S. government are classified. This is the rationale for the Galileo Project, which under my leadership aims to resolve the nature of UAP by constructing dedicated new observatories. Astronomical observatories focus on a small portion of the sky at any given time and ignore objects that maneuver in the Earth’s atmosphere and hence are different from meteors. The existing Galileo Observatories offer a new architecture whereby a set of infrared cameras, visible-light cameras, radio sensors and acoustic microphones monitor the entire sky at all times. A new paper reporting the first triangulation results from the Galileo research team will be shared with the public shortly. The Galileo Project is currently designing its fourth observatory in Carl Sagan’s old residence in Ithaca, New York. The design of this observatory will be unique, aiming to resolve UAP orbs by imaging them at high resolution and taking their spectrum to infer their composition. The orb imager observatory concept was described here.

***

In pursuing the government archives path, the UAP Science Advisory Council under my leadership is collaborating the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office in the Pentagon (AARO), the FBI, the Intelligence Community and the White House, following President Trump’s directive here. The council studies data that was released through the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE). It also recommends the collection of new data by placing new sensors in locations where UAPs were reported by government and military personnel.

We are all hoping that the volume of available data will increase considerably thanks to the memo issued on July 31, 2026 by the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, Aaron Lukas. I applaud the leadership of Aaron Lukas and everyone working to make full UAP disclosure possible. We are arriving at a moment of truth for UAP whistleblowers who argued over the years that they are legally refrained from revealing federal secrets by non-disclosure agreements (NDAs). People with relevant knowledge are encouraged to come forward and usher in a new era of UAP disclosure. The UAP Science Advisory Council is ready to work with whistleblowers and government partners to independently evaluate the evidence and help verify the science wherever the data leads.

Today, Aaron Lukas tweeted:

“I’d like to thank Professor Avi Loeb and the UAP Science Advisory Council, as well as “The Disclosure Foundation” and “To the Stars” representatives, for joining us recently at @ODNIgov in their capacity as advisors to the intelligence community’s UAP Governance Board. Your insights and feedback into @POTUS’s historic disclosure effort are appreciated and the American people are fortunate to have such expert counsel. We look forward to continued collaboration on PURSUE objectives.”

To which I replied:

“On behalf of the UAP Science Advisory Council (@UAPSAC), I would like to thank Deputy Director of National Intelligence @DepDNILukas and ODNI for their support and hospitality as we collaborate on resolving the nature of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena. It is a great privilege and pleasure to work with them. — Avi Loeb”

***

Stay tuned as we bring clarity on the nature of UAP. The best is yet to come. We all deserve to know the truth on whether we have neighbors among the stars. This offers a golden opportunity for the U.S. to lead the way in the next chapter of human history.

ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Avi Loeb is chair of the UAP Science Advisory Council to the White House, Pentagon, FBI and intelligence agencies, director of the Galileo Project, founding director of Harvard University’s — Black Hole Initiative, former director of the Institute for Theory and Computation at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics, and the former chair of the astronomy department at Harvard University (2011–2020). He is a former member of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology and a former chair of the Board on Physics and Astronomy of the National Academies. He is the bestselling author of “Extraterrestrial: The First Sign of Intelligent Life Beyond Earth” and a co-author of the textbook “Life in the Cosmos”, both published in 2021. The paperback edition of his new book, titled “Interstellar”, was published in August 2024.
